process_issues.description: api_server vitest reported a one-off failure inside `ai-workflow checks --level pr` while a live smoke app (api_server :4001 + opencode :4096) was running; a standalone `npx vitest run` passed 542/542 and a clean harness re-run passed. Likely resource/port contention between the live smoke app and the test run, not a code regression.
process_issues.detected_by: ai-workflow checks --level pr vitest ✗ then standalone npx vitest run 542/542 ✓ and harness re-run ✓.

issues.description: verification-gate emitted PASS for #645 on the strength of green widget tests TWICE, but the behavioral-evidence rule was satisfied only at the widget level (AgentKindBadgeTestHarness), not at the user-visible level. Round 1 was a false-green (the contract test fed providerId='codex', an agent-kind the app never stores; production stores the LLM provider 'openai'/'google'). Round 2 passed verification but manual smoke found the badge wrong in 3 of 4 render sites because the contract tested the widget in isolation, not the composing views (_TranscriptHeader, _ResumableSessionRow, agent_bubble_overlay). Both are upstream acceptance-contract gaps that verification-gate's behavioral-evidence rule did not flag as insufficient.
issues.detected_by: Orchestrator trust-but-verify caught round 1 (compared the test's injected value to the value _applyPick actually stores); manual smoke caught round 2.

suggested_follow_up: Sharpen acceptance-contract: for UI/widget changes, enumerate EVERY render site of the changed widget and assert each composing view; and require contract test inputs to be the value the production code path actually produces (not a convenient stand-in). Sharpen verification-gate behavioral-evidence rule: a widget-isolation test is insufficient evidence when the widget renders in multiple parent views.
